+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Distance
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.DistributionAux
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.State
+
+/-! # State-dependent consistency and strategy closeness
+
+The definitions are the finite-dimensional forms of `def:consistency` and
+`def:strategy-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:180-220`,
+from `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+/-- Off-diagonal consistency defect for two operator families on a state. -/
+noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
+  avgOver μ (fun x =>
+    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
+      if a = b then 0 else
+        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
+          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)
+
+/-- The relation `A ≃_δ B` from `def:consistency`. -/
+def IsConsistentWithin {X α ι : Type*}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=
+  consistencyDefect μ A B ψ ≤ δ
+
+/-- Operator distance with a unit answer alphabet, used for sums of effects. -/
+noncomputable def opDistSq {X ι : Type*}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
+  opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x) (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ
+
+theorem opDistSq_eq_opFamilyDistSq {X ι : Type*}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
+    opDistSq μ M N ψ = opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x)
+      (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ := rfl
+
+/-- Explicit transports and quantitative bounds for close bundled strategies. -/
+structure AreCloseStrategies (G : Game)
+    {ιA ιB ιA' ιB' : Type*}
+    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA'] [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB))
+    (ψ' : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB'))
+    (A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA)
+    (A' : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA')
+    (B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB)
+    (B' : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB') (δ : ℝ) where
+  transportA : ιA ≃ ιA'
+  transportB : ιB ≃ ιB'
+  state : stateDistSq ψ (reindexState
+      (Equiv.prodCongr transportA.symm transportB.symm) ψ') ≤ δ
+  alice : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.fst)
+      (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).effect a) 1)
+      (fun x a => heteroKron (reindexOp transportA ((A' x).effect a)) 1) ψ ≤ δ
+  bob : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.snd)
+      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 ((B y).effect b))

+import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.Distribution
+
+/-! # Finite distribution combinators -/
+
+open scoped BigOperators
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT
+
+/-- Product of two finite distributions, with multiplicative weights. -/
+noncomputable def Distribution.prod {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
+    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β) : Distribution (α × β) where
+  support := μ.support.product ν.support
+  weight p := μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2
+  nonnegative p := mul_nonneg (μ.nonnegative p.1) (ν.nonnegative p.2)
+  outsideSupport p hp := by
+    by_cases hμ : p.1 ∈ μ.support
+    · have hν : p.2 ∉ ν.support := by
+        intro h
+        exact hp (Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨hμ, h⟩)
+      simp [ν.outsideSupport p.2 hν]
+    · simp [μ.outsideSupport p.1 hμ]
+
+/-- Convex mixture of two finite distributions. -/
+noncomputable def Distribution.mix {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
+    (t : ℝ) (μ ν : Distribution α) : Distribution α where
+  support := μ.support ∪ ν.support
+  weight a := |t| * μ.weight a + |1 - t| * ν.weight a
+  nonnegative a := by
+    exact add_nonneg (mul_nonneg (abs_nonneg _) (μ.nonnegative a))
+      (mul_nonneg (abs_nonneg _) (ν.nonnegative a))
+  outsideSupport a ha := by
+    have hμ : a ∉ μ.support := fun h => ha (Finset.mem_union_left _ h)
+    have hν : a ∉ ν.support := fun h => ha (Finset.mem_union_right _ h)
+    simp [μ.outsideSupport a hμ, ν.outsideSupport a hν]
+
+/-- A dependent finite bind over a distribution-valued family. -/
+noncomputable def Distribution.bind {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
+    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : α → Distribution β) : Distribution β where
+  support := μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support)
+  weight b := ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * (ν a).weight b
+  nonnegative b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => mul_nonneg (μ.nonnegative a) ((ν a).nonnegative b)
+  outsideSupport b hb := by
+    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
+    intro a ha
+    have hnot : b ∉ (ν a).support := by
+      intro h
+      exact hb (Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨a, ha, h⟩)
+    simp [ν a |>.outsideSupport b hnot]
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

+import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.ParametersBase

+/-! # Polynomial error predicates -/
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+/-- `IsPolyErr f` means that `f` is a polynomially bounded error function. -/
+def IsPolyErr (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ C r : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ 0 ≤ r ∧ ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C * (1 + |x|) ^ r
+
+/-- Two-parameter version of the polynomial error predicate. -/
+def IsPolyErr2 (f : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ C r s : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ 0 ≤ r ∧ 0 ≤ s ∧
+    ∀ x y, |f x y| ≤ C * (1 + |x|) ^ r * (1 + |y|) ^ s
+
+abbrev IsPolyErr₂ := IsPolyErr2
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Defs
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Consistency
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.State
+
+/-! # Strategy classes and symmetric games
+
+This module defines projective, commuting, consistent, PCC, and SPCC strategy
+predicates from `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:90-170`, with source
+definitions in `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:58-218`.
+-/
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+/-- A tensor-product strategy is projective when both answer measurements are. -/
+def Strategy.IsProjective {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : Prop :=
+  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.A x)) ∧
+    ∀ y, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.B y)
+
+/-- A symmetric game has one question and answer alphabet and symmetric data. -/
+structure SymmetricGame where
+  Question : Type
+  Answer : Type
+  [questionFintype : Fintype Question]
+  [answerFintype : Fintype Answer]
+  [questionDecidableEq : DecidableEq Question]
+  [answerDecidableEq : DecidableEq Answer]
+  μ : Distribution (Question × Question)
+  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
+  μ_symm : ∀ x y, μ.weight (x, y) = μ.weight (y, x)
+  decide : Question → Question → Answer → Answer → Bool
+  decide_symm : ∀ x y a b, decide x y a b = decide y x b a
+
+attribute [instance] SymmetricGame.questionFintype SymmetricGame.answerFintype
+  SymmetricGame.questionDecidableEq SymmetricGame.answerDecidableEq
+
+/-- Forget symmetry and view a symmetric game as a general game. -/
+def SymmetricGame.toGame (G : SymmetricGame) : Game where
+  QuestionA := G.Question
+  QuestionB := G.Question
+  AnswerA := G.Answer
+  AnswerB := G.Answer
+  μ := G.μ
+  μ_prob := G.μ_prob
+  decide := G.decide
+
+/-- A strategy for a symmetric game uses one local space and one measurement family. -/
+structure SymmetricStrategy (G : SymmetricGame) where
+  ι : Type
+  [ιFintype : Fintype ι]
+  [ιDecidableEq : DecidableEq ι]
+  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)
+  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
+  ψ_swap : reindexState (Equiv.prodComm ι ι) ψ = ψ
+  M : G.Question → Measurement G.Answer ι
+
+attribute [instance] SymmetricStrategy.ιFintype SymmetricStrategy.ιDecidableEq
+
+/-- Forget the symmetry witness and obtain a general tensor-product strategy. -/
+def SymmetricStrategy.toStrategy {G : SymmetricGame} (S : SymmetricStrategy G) :
+    Strategy G.toGame where
+  ιA := S.ι
+  ιB := S.ι
+  ψ := S.ψ
+  ψ_norm := S.ψ_norm
+  A := S.M
+  B := S.M
+
+/-- Commutation of two measurement families on a common local space. -/
+def IsCommutingOn {X α β ι : Type*}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β]
+    [DecidableEq β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → α → Op ι) (B : X → β → Op ι) : Prop :=
+  ∀ x, 0 < μ.weight x → ∀ a b, Commute (A x a) (B x b)
+
+/-- A strategy is commuting when its local spaces can be identified and the
+transported measurement families commute on the support. -/
+def Strategy.IsCommuting {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : Prop :=
+  ∃ e : S.ιA ≃ S.ιB,
+    IsCommutingOn G.μ
+      (fun xy a => (S.A xy.1).effect a)
+      (fun xy b => reindexOp e ((S.B xy.2).effect b))
+
+/-- Consistency of one measurement on a bipartite state. -/
+def Measurement.IsConsistentOn {α ι : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (M : Measurement α ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) : Prop :=
+  ∀ a, (heteroKron (M.effect a) 1).mulVec ψ =
+    (heteroKron 1 (M.effect a)).mulVec ψ
+
+/-- Consistency of both families of a general strategy on a common state. -/
+def IsConsistentStrategyOn {α β ι : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (A : α → Measurement β ι) (B : α → Measurement β ι)
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) : Prop :=
+  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (A x) ψ) ∧
+    ∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (B x) ψ
+
+/-- Consistency for a symmetric strategy. -/
+def SymmetricStrategy.IsConsistent {G : SymmetricGame}
+    (S : SymmetricStrategy G) : Prop :=
+  ∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (S.M x) S.ψ
+
+/-- Projective, consistent, commuting strategy predicate on a common space. -/
+def Strategy.IsPCC {G : Game} {ι : Type*}
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (μ : Distribution (G.QuestionA × G.QuestionB))
+    (A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ι)
+    (B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ι)
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) : Prop :=
+  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (A x)) ∧
+    (∀ y, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (B y)) ∧
+    (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (A x) ψ) ∧
+    (∀ y, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (B y) ψ) ∧
+      IsCommutingOn μ (fun xy a => (A xy.1).effect a)
+        (fun xy b => (B xy.2).effect b)
+
+/-- Symmetric projective, consistent, commuting predicate. -/
+def SymmetricStrategy.IsSPCC {G : SymmetricGame}
+    (S : SymmetricStrategy G) : Prop :=
+  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.M x)) ∧ S.IsConsistent ∧
+    IsCommutingOn G.μ (fun xy a => (S.M xy.1).effect a)
+      (fun xy b => (S.M xy.2).effect b)
+
+/-- Source symmetrization statement; attainment remains a proof obligation. -/
+theorem exists_symmetric_projective_strategy (G : SymmetricGame) (ε : ℝ)
+    (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (h : G.toGame.value = 1 - ε) :
+    ∃ S : SymmetricStrategy G, S.toStrategy.IsProjective ∧
+      1 - ε ≤ S.toStrategy.value := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Established symmetrization from a concrete strategy, used by downstream proofs. -/
+theorem exists_symmetric_projective_strategy_of_strategy (G : SymmetricGame)
+    (ε : ℝ) (S₀ : Strategy G.toGame) (h : 1 - ε ≤ S₀.value) :
+    ∃ S : SymmetricStrategy G, S.toStrategy.IsProjective ∧
+      1 - ε ≤ S.toStrategy.value := by
+  sorry
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

+import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.Basic

+/-!
+# Neutral finite-dimensional state constructions
+
+This leaf contains tensor and reindexing operations shared by the QPBT game and
+test layers.  The definitions support the state transports used in the Pauli
+basis test (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
+-/
+
+open scoped Matrix
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+/-- Conjugate a finite operator by a linear isometry. -/
+noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
+    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
+    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
+  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
+  U * M * Uᴴ
+
+/-- Reindex a finite Euclidean-space vector along an equivalence. -/
+noncomputable def reindexState {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (e : ι ≃ ι')
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι' :=
+  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm
+    (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))
+
+/-- Apply two local isometries to a bipartite state, with arbitrary finite
+codomain index types. -/
+noncomputable def isometryTensor
+    {ιA ιB κA κB R : Type*}
+    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
+    [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
+    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × R))
+    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (κB × R))
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
+    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((κA × R) × (κB × R)) :=
+  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((κA × R) × (κB × R)) ℂ).symm
+    (fun p =>
+      ∑ i : ιA, ∑ j : ιB,
+        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (κA × R) ℂ)
+            (φA ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιA ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) p.1) *
+          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (κB × R) ℂ)
+            (φB ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιB ℂ).symm (Pi.single j 1))) p.2) *
+          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA × ιB) ℂ) ψ (i, j)))
+
+/-- Tensor two real coordinate vectors, indexed by a product. -/
+def vecTensor {ι κ : Type*} (u : ι → ℝ) (v : κ → ℝ) : ι × κ → ℝ :=
+  fun p => u p.1 * v p.2
+
+/-- Reindex a finite matrix along equivalences of its row and column types. -/
+def reindexOp {ι ι' : Type*} (e : ι ≃ ι') (M : Op ι') : Op ι :=
+  (Matrix.reindex e.symm e.symm) M
+
+/-- The four-factor product shuffle used to compare bipartite tensor orderings. -/
+def prodShuffle {α β γ δ : Type*} :
+    (α × β) × (γ × δ) ≃ (α × γ) × (β × δ) where
+  toFun p := ((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2, p.2.2))
+  invFun p := ((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2, p.2.2))
+  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
+  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     2	\label{sec:linear}
     3	
     4	\subsection{Conditionally linear functions and distributions}
     5	\label{sec:cl}
     6	
     7	We first introduce \emph{conditionally linear functions}, which are used to
     8	specify the question distribution for games considered in the paper in a way
     9	that the question distribution can be ``introspected'', as described in
    10	Section~\ref{sec:introspection}.
    11	Intuitively, a conditionally linear function takes as input an element
    12	$x\in V = \F^n$ for some $n\geq 0$, and applies linear maps $L_j$ sequentially
    13	on $x^{V_j}$ where $V_1,V_2,\ldots $ are a sequence of complementary register
    14	subspaces such that both the linear maps $L_j$ and the subspace $V_j$ for
    15	$j \ge 2$ may depend on the values taken by previous linear maps $L_1(x^{V_1})$,
    16	$L_2(x^{V_2})$, etc.
    17	
    18	In the remainder of the section we use $V$ to denote the linear space $\F^n$ for
    19	some integer $n \geq 0$.
    20	For ease of notation we extensively use the subscript range notation.
    21	For example, if $V_1, V_2, \ldots, V_\ell$ are fixed subspaces of $V$ and $k \in
    22	\{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ we write
    23	\begin{equation*}
    24	  V_{<k} = \bigoplus_{j\,:\,1 \le j<k} V_j\;,\quad
    25	  V_{> k} = \bigoplus_{j\,:\, \ell\ge j > k} V_j\;,
    26	\end{equation*}
    27	and it is understood that $V_{\le k}$ and $V_{\ge k}$ are identical to
    28	$V_{<k+1}$ and $V_{>k-1}$, respectively.
    29	Moreover, if $V'$ is a register subspace of $V$, $F: V' \to V'$ is a function,
    30	and $x \in V$, we write $x^F$ to denote $F(x^{V'})$.
    31	For example, in the following definition $x^{L_1}$ is used as shorthand notation
    32	for $L_1(x^{V_1})$.
    33	
    34	
    35	\begin{definition}
    36	  \label{def:cl-func}
    37		Let $V$ be $\F^n$ for some $n\geq 0$.
    38	  For all integers $\ell\geq 0$ the collection of \emph{$\ell$-level
    39	    conditionally linear functions} (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is defined
    40	  inductively as follows.
    41	  \begin{enumerate}
    42	  \item There is a single $0$-level conditionally linear function, which is the
    43	    $0$ function on $V$.
    44	
    45	  \item Let $\ell \geq 1$ and suppose the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level
    46	    conditionally linear functions has been defined.
    47	    The collection of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions on $V$ consists
    48	    of all functions $L$ on $V$ that can be expressed in the following form.
    49	    There exist complementary register subspaces $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ of $V$, a
    50	    linear function $L_1$ on $V_1$, and for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$, an
    51	    $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear function $L_{>1,\, v}$ on $V_{>1}$,
    52	    such that for all $x\in V$,
    53	    \begin{equation*}
    54	      L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}} (x^{V_{>1}})\;.
    55	    \end{equation*}
    56	  \end{enumerate}
    57	\end{definition}
    58	
    59	The concept of conditionally linear functions is simple even though the
    60	notations seem complicated.
    61	It is best understood using an operational definition illustrated in
    62	\cref{fig:cl-functions}.
    63	We give an example of a $2$-level CL function in \cref{ex:cl-function}.
    64	
    65	\begin{remark}
    66	  \label{rk:level-1-is-linear}
    67	  It follows from the above definition that all $1$-level CL functions are linear.
    68	\end{remark}
    69	
    70	\begin{example}\label{ex:cl-function}
    71	Consider $V = \F_{2}^{3}$. Then the following map
    72	\begin{equation*}
    73	  L:(x_{0}, x_{1}, x_{2})
    74	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0},  x_{2})
    75	\end{equation*}
    76	on $V$ is a $2$-level CL function by choosing $V_{1} = \mathrm{span}\{(0,0,1)\}$, $L_{1}$
    77	the identity function on $V_{1}$, $V_{2} = V_{1}^{\perp}$, and
    78	\begin{equation*}
    79	  L_{2,\, x_{2}}: (x_{0}, x_{1}, 0)
    80	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0}, 0),
    81	\end{equation*}
    82	which is linear for all $x_{2} \in \F_{2}$.
    83	Note that intuitively the function $L$ selects either $x_{0}$ or $x_{1}$ in the
    84	second coordinate conditioning on the value of $x_{2}$.
    85	\end{example}

   276	\begin{definition}[Line-point distributions]
   277	        \label{def:line-point-dist}
   278	 The \emph{axis line-point distribution} $D_{\ALine}$ is the
   279	 distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$ over pairs $(\ell=(u_0,e_i),u)$

   282	 $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$  over $(\ell=(u_0,s,v),u)$. The
   283	 \emph{line-point distribution} $D_{\Line}$ is the equal mixture of the axis-parallel line-point distribution and the diagonal line-point distribution.

   285	 with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\ALine}$,

    60	\begin{remark}
    61	  Unless specified otherwise, all strategies considered in this paper are tensor
    62	  product strategies, and we simply call them \emph{strategies}.
    63	  Similarly, we refer to $\val^*(\game)$ as the \emph{value} of the game
    64	  $\game$.
    65	\end{remark}

    67	
    68	\begin{definition}[Projective strategies]
    69	  \label{def:projective-strategy}
    70	  We say that a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ is \emph{projective} if
    71	  all the measurements $\{A^x_a\}_a$ and $\{B^y_b\}_b$ are projective.
    72	\end{definition}
    73	
    74	\begin{definition}\label{rem:symmetric-games}
    75		A game $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is
    76	  \emph{symmetric} if the question and answer alphabets are the same for both
    77	  players (i.e.\
    78	  $\cal{X} = \cal{Y}$ and $\cal{A} = \cal{B}$), the distribution $\mu$ is
    79	  symmetric (i.e.\
    80	  $\mu(x,y) = \mu(y,x)$), and the decision predicate $D$ treats both players
    81	  symmetrically (i.e.\ for all $x,y,a,b$, $D(x,y,a,b) = D(y,x,b,a)$).
    82	 
    83	We call a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$
    84	  \emph{symmetric} if $\ket{\psi}$ is a (pure) state in $\mH \otimes \mH$, for some
    85	  Hilbert space $\mH$, that is invariant under permutation of the two factors,
    86	  and the measurement operators of both players are identical.
    87	\end{definition}
    88	
    89	We often specify symmetric games $\game$ and symmetric strategies $\strategy$ using
    90	  a compact notation: we write $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A}, \mu, D)$ and
    91	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ where $M$ denotes the set of measurement
    92	  operators for both players.
    93	
    94	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:symmetric-strat}
    95	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A},  \mu, D)$ be a symmetric game
    96	  such that $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some $\eps\geq 0$.
    97	  Then there exists a symmetric and projective strategy
    98	  $\strategy=(\ket{\psi},M)$ such that $\val^*(\game,\strategy)\geq 1-\eps$.
    99	\end{lemma}
   100	
   101	\begin{proof}
   102	  By definition for any $\eps'>\eps$ there exists a strategy $\strategy'= (\ket{\psi'},A,B)$ such
   103	  that $\val^*(\game,\strategy')\geq 1-\eps'$.
   104	Using Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}) we can assume
   105	without loss of generality that $\ket{\psi'}\in\C_{\alice'}^d\otimes \C_{\bob'}^d$ for some integer $d$
   106	  and that for every $x$, $A^x$ and $B^x$ are projective measurements.
   107	Let
   108	  \[
   109	    \ket{\psi} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \big( \ket{0}_\alice \ket{1}_\bob
   110	    \ket{\psi'}_{\alice'\bob'} + \ket{1}_\alice \ket{0}_\bob
   111	    \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{\alice'\bob'}\big) \in (\C_{\alice}^2 \otimes
   112	    \C_{\alice'}^d) \otimes (\C_\bob^2 \otimes \C_{\bob'}^d)\;,
   113	  \]
   114	  where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ is obtained from $\ket{\psi}$ by permuting the two
   115	  players' registers.
   116	  Observe that $\ket{\psi}$ is invariant under permutation of $\alice\alice'$
   117	  and $\bob\bob'$.
   118	
   119	  For any question $x\in \cal{X}$ define the measurement $M^x = \{M^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$
   120	  acting on the Hilbert space $\C^2 \otimes \C^d$ as follows:
   121	  \[
   122	  	M^x_a = \ketbra{0}{0} \otimes A^x_a + \ketbra{1}{1} \otimes B^x_a \;,
   123	  \]
   124		i.e.\ for $\ket{\varphi} \in \C^d$, $M^x_a(\ket{0}\ket{\varphi})=\ket{0}A^x_a\ket{\varphi}$ and $M^x_a(\ket{1}\ket{\varphi})=\ket{1}B^x_a\ket{\varphi}$.
   125	  When Alice receives question $x$, she measures $M^x$ on registers $\alice \alice'$, and when Bob receives 
   126	  question $y$, he measures $M^y$ on registers $\bob \bob'$.
   127	Using that by assumption the decision predicate $D$ for $\game$ is symmetric,
   128	  it is not hard to verify that $\val^*(\game,\strategy) =
   129	  \val^*(\game,\strategy')$.
   130	\end{proof}

   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:comm-strategy}
   134	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ be a game, and let
   135	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a strategy for $\game$ such that  $\mH_A = \mH_B$.
   136	  Let $S \subseteq \cal{X} \times \cal{Y}$ denote the support of the question
   137	  distribution $\mu$, i.e.\ the set of $(x,y)$ such that $\mu(x,y)>0$.
   138	  We say that $\strategy$ is a \emph{commuting strategy for $\game$} if for all
   139	  question pairs $(x, y) \in S$, we have $[A^x_a, B^y_b] = 0$ 
   140	  for all $a
   141	  \in \cal{A}, b \in \cal{B}$, where $[A, B] = AB - BA$ denotes the commutator.
   142	\end{definition}
   143	
   144	\begin{definition}[Consistent measurements]
   145	  \label{def:consistent-measurement}
   146	  Let $\cal{A}$ be a finite set, let $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$ be a
   147	  state, and let $\{ M_a \}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ be a projective measurement on
   148	  $\mH$.
   149	  We say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$} if
   150	  and only if
   151	  \begin{equation*}
   152	    \forall a \in \mA\;,\quad M_a \otimes \Id_\bob\, \ket{\psi}
   153	    = \Id_\alice \otimes M_a\, \ket{\psi}\;.
   154	  \end{equation*}
   155		When the state $\ket{\psi}$ is clear from context we simply say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent}.
   156	\end{definition}
   157	
   158	The terminology ``consistent'' arises from the fact that when the measurement $\{M_a\}$ is performed on both registers of $\ket{\psi}$, the probability of obtaining twice the same outcome is 
   159	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes (M_a)^2 \ket{\psi} \,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} \,=\,1\;,\]
   160	where the first equality is by definition of consistency, the second uses that $\{M_a\}$ is projective, and the last uses $\sum_a M_a=\Id$. 
   161	
   162	\begin{definition}[Consistent strategies]
   163	  \label{def:consistent-strategy}
   164		Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a projective strategy with state
   165	  $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$, for some Hilbert space~$\mH$, which is
   166	  defined on question alphabets $\cal{X}$ and~$\cal{Y}$ and answer alphabets
   167	  $\cal{A}$ and~$\cal{B}$, respectively.
   168	  We say that the strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{consistent} if for all $x \in
   169	  \cal{X}$, the measurement $\{A^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on
   170	  $\ket{\psi}$ and if for all $y \in \cal{Y}$, the measurement $\{B^y_b\}_{b \in
   171	    \cal{B}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$.
   172	\end{definition}
   173	
   174	We almost always restrict our attention to symmetric strategies. In this case, consistency implies that whenever both players are sent the same question, they provide the same answer. 
   175	
   176	\begin{definition}
   177	  \label{def:spcc}
   178	  We say that a strategy $\strategy$ for a game $\game$ is \emph{PCC} if it is projective, consistent, and commuting for $\game$.
   179	  Additionally, we say that a PCC strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{SPCC} if it is furthermore symmetric.
   180	\end{definition}

   183	Recall that for a (pure) state $\ket{\psi}\in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$, the \emph{Schmidt rank} of $\ket{\psi}$ is the smallest integer $k$ such that 
   184	\[ \ket{\psi} = \sum_{i=1}^k\, \alpha_i \ket{u_i}\otimes \ket{v_i}\;,\]
   185	for some orthonormal families $\{\ket{u_i}\}\subset \mH_\alice$ and $\{\ket{v_i}\}\subset\mH_\bob$ and $\alpha_i>0$. The coefficients $\alpha_i$ are uniquely defined by $\ket{\psi}$ and called \emph{Schmidt coefficients}. The state $\ket{\psi}$ is called \emph{maximally entangled} if $\alpha_i=\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}}$ for all $i=1,\ldots,k$.

   187	
   188	\begin{definition}[Entanglement requirements of a game]
   189	  \label{def:ent}
   190		For all games $\game$ and $\nu \in [0, 1]$, let $\Ent(\game, \nu)$ denote the
   191	  minimum integer $d$ such that there exists a finite dimensional tensor product
   192	  strategy $\strategy$ that achieves success probability at least $\nu$ in the
   193	  game $\game$ with a state $\ket{\psi}$ whose Schmidt rank is at most $d$.
   194	  If there is no finite dimensional strategy that achieves success probability
   195	  $\nu$, then define $\Ent(\game, \nu)$ to be $\infty$.
   196	\end{definition}

   200	\begin{remark}
   201	  A strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ for a symmetric game $\game =
   202	  (\cal{X}, \cal{X}, \cal{A}, \cal{A}, \mu, D)$ is called \emph{synchronous} if
   203	  it holds that for every $x\in \cal{X}$ and $a\neq b \in \cal{A}$, $\bra{\psi}
   204	  A^x_a \otimes B^x_b \ket{\psi} = 0$; in other words,
   205	  the players never return different answers when simultaneously asked the same
   206	  question.
   207	  As shown in~\cite{paulsen2016estimating} the condition for a
   208	  finite-dimensional strategy of being synchronous is equivalent to the
   209	  condition that it is projective, consistent, and moreover $\ket{\psi}$ is a
   210	  maximally entangled state.
   211	  (The equivalence is extended to infinite-dimensional strategies, as well as
   212	  correlations induced by limits of finite-dimensional strategies,
   213	  in~\cite{kim2018synchronous}.)
   214	\end{remark}
   215	\subsection{Distance measures}
   216	
   217	We introduce several distance measures that are used throughout.
   218	
   219	\begin{definition}[Distance between states]
   220	  \label{def:state-distance}
   221	
   222		Let $\{\ket{\psi_n}\}_{n\in \N}$ and $\{\ket{\psi'_n}\}_{n\in \N}$ be two
   223	  families of states in the same space $\mH$.

  mkdir -p "$LOCK_DIR"
